facts.text: New Holland birthed the New Holland Machine Company in 1895, founded by Abe Zimmerman, which later evolved into New Holland Agriculture.
The town’s community band, founded in 1829, has played continuously since 1856, even performing at the Eiffel Tower and for President Lincoln.
The New Holland Band Museum, tucked inside the Eastern Lancaster County Library, showcases more than 150 instruments and Sousa-era uniforms.
Railroad service arrived in New Holland in 1876, linking the town to Downingtown and spurring local commerce.
The New Holland Area Historical Society, at 207 E Main St., preserves thousands of historic photos and hosts public meetings.
The New Holland Machine Company building shares National Register of Historic Places status with the John Casper Stoever Log House.
